text:
Kyle Palmieri has three goals in 17 games and none in his last six, and if you only watched the scoresheet you would think the 35-year-old Long Islander was fading. The chances say otherwise. He has 5.67 individual expected goals, more than anyone on the Islanders in this group, and with him on the ice at 5v5 they have 54% of expected goals, five and a half points better than without him.

So far it has not gone in. He is shooting 8% against a usual range near 12%, and the team has scored five fewer goals than its chances deserved with him out there. Both of those tend to swing back, which is why our numbers flag him as due.

The quality of looks is no accident. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small eight-game sample last season, had him taking 2.8 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the most dangerous kind. He missed much of last year, so the Islanders are leaning on a player still finding his rhythm. Five points is a low floor for what he is doing.
headline: Palmieri keeps getting the looks, and missing
